target: Set.finite_div, Set.infinite_div (`variable [DivisionMonoid α] [IsLeftCancelMul α] [IsRightCancelMul α]`, Set/Finite.lean 139), and the DivisionMonoid-level div lemmas generally
claim: In a `DivisionMonoid`, left and right cancellation are equivalent: inversion reverses products and is injective. So `finite_div` / `infinite_div` assume a redundant second mixin. Meanwhile a client holding one mixin cannot use them, nor `card_le_card_div_right`, nor the simp lemma `div_left_inj`, although every one of these statements holds for it. Neither the PR nor the base has a lemma bridging the two mixins in this setting. `Defs.lean` has the analogous bridge for the commutative case.
requested_change: Add, next to `div_right_inj` in Basic.lean, `@[to_additive] lemma DivisionMonoid.IsLeftCancelMul.toIsRightCancelMul (G) [DivisionMonoid G] [IsLeftCancelMul G] : IsRightCancelMul G` and its converse. Model them on `CommMagma.IsLeftCancelMul.toIsRightCancelMul` (lemmas, not instances). Then state `Set.finite_div` / `Set.infinite_div` under the single mixin `[DivisionMonoid α] [IsLeftCancelMul α]`, deriving the other through the bridge. If the bridge is not wanted, at least assume the bundled `[IsCancelMul α]`.
evidence: Both bridge directions compile in four lines each, and each left/right partner of the Basic.lean family is derivable from the other under the opposite mixin (c12). With the bridge, `finite_div` and `infinite_div` compile under `[DivisionMonoid R] [IsLeftCancelMul R]` alone (c34). Without it, the existing proof fails for that context (c32), and a one-mixin client fails on `infinite_div` (c31), on `card_le_card_div_right` (c27) and on `simpa` via `div_left_inj` (c13); supplying the bridge by `haveI` fixes the latter (c14). The CommMagma precedent is in c37, and the binder census (pair spelling 2 uses, both in this file; `[IsCancelMul _]` 26 uses in 21 files) is in c35.
